3. This Witness Statement addresses Questions 7(b), 8, 9(a), 9(c) and 9(d) of the 4 February Letter. Other Questions which are within the FSD’s purview will be addressed in the witness statements of other relevant officers of the FSD to the Committee. I understand that the FSD has indexed all relevant documents in its possession in Lists of Documents produced on various dates (collectively “LoD”). In this Witness Statement, I shall refer to these documents by their designation in the LoD (for example, [FSD/A(I)/1] means Item 1 in Part A(I) of the LoD, [FSD(2)/A(I)/1] means Item 1 in Part A(I) of the 2nd LoD, and so on) without annexing them hereto for the avoidance of duplication.

4. This Witness Statement describes (i) the circumstances in which communications with Senior Fireman (Posthumous) 18469 HO Wai-ho (“SFn HO”) became lost and the search and rescue operations which were conducted to locate SFn HO in answer to Question 7(b); and (ii) the decisions made by me as the Incident Commander after the fire was upgraded to No. 3 Alarm in answer to Questions 8, 9(a), 9(c) and 9(d). The response should be read together with the timeline and account of the No. 3 Alarm Fire provided in paragraphs 18 to 29 of the Witness Statement of TANG Wing-wah.

[Questions 8 and 9(a)]
5. As stated in paragraph 19 of the Witness Statement of TANG Wing-wah, I was the second of the two Incident Commanders of the No. 3 Alarm Fire (from 1502 hours to 1533 hours). At 1508 hours on 26.11.2025, I received a telephone call from the Fire Services Communications Centre, which instructed me to attend a No.3 Alarm Fire at Wang Cheong House, Wang Fuk Court.
